title: Introduction
text: In this tutorial, you will build a full-stack React app using FormCMS and VS Code with Codex — without writing a single line of backend code.

title: Step 1: Start Backend
text: Step 1: Start the FormCMS backend. Run this Docker command in your terminal. It exposes port 5000 for the REST API, the admin portal, and the built-in MCP server.

title: Step 1: Admin Setup
text: Open localhost 5000 slash mate. Follow the setup wizard to create your super admin account.

title: Step 1: API Key
text: Next, go to Settings, then API Key Configuration, and click Generate. Copy this key — you will need it in the next step.

title: Step 2: MCP Config
text: Step 2: Connect Codex to FormCMS. In VS Code, create a dot vscode slash mcp dot json file. Add the FormCMS MCP server entry using supergateway as a local bridge. Paste your API key where shown.

title: Step 3: AI Skill
text: Step 3: Add the AI instruction file. Run this curl command to download the FormCMS skill file into your project. This teaches Codex how to use FormCMS APIs — schema design, data seeding, and deployment.

title: Step 4: Scaffold
text: Step 4: Scaffold the project. Open the Codex panel in VS Code and type this prompt. Codex will create a Vite plus React app, configure the proxy, define your schema entities, seed sample data, and start the dev server — all automatically.

title: Step 5: Frontend
text: Step 5: Build the frontend. Ask Codex to build components like PostList and PostDetail. Because Codex already knows your schema from the MCP tools, it uses the correct field names automatically.

title: Step 6: Deploy
text: Step 6: Deploy. Tell Codex to build and deploy as the home page. It runs npm run build, zips the output, and calls the deploy SPA MCP tool. Your full-stack app is now live from a single container.

title: Conclusion
text: That is it. You now have a full-stack React application — schema, data, frontend, and deployment — built entirely through Codex in VS Code. No manual backend work required.
